```{r}
library(changepoint)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Fonction pour appliquer cpt.meanvar avec différentes pénalités
apply_cpt_meanvar <- function(data, penalties) {
  results <- list()
  for (penalty in penalties) {
    tryCatch({
      changepoint <- cpt.meanvar(data, method = "PELT", penalty = penalty)
      results[[penalty]] <- changepoint
    }, error = function(e) {
      message(sprintf("Error with penalty %s: %s", penalty, e$message))
    })
  }
  return(results)
}

# Fonction pour évaluer la qualité du modèle
evaluate_model <- function(data, changepoint) {
  segments <- cpts(changepoint)
  n <- length(data)
  
  # Calculer la somme des carrés des résidus
  rss <- sum((data - rep(param.est(changepoint)$mean, diff(c(0, segments, n))))^2)
  
  # Calculer le BIC
  k <- length(segments) + 1  # nombre de segments
  bic <- n * log(rss/n) + k * log(n)
  
  # Calculer l'AIC
  aic <- n * log(rss/n) + 2 * k
  
  return(list(rss = rss, bic = bic, aic = aic, num_changes = k-1))
}

# Fonction principale
analyze_changepoints <- function(data, penalties) {
  # Appliquer cpt.meanvar avec différentes pénalités
  results <- apply_cpt_meanvar(data, penalties)
  
  # Évaluer chaque modèle
  evaluations <- lapply(results, function(x) evaluate_model(data, x))
  
  # Créer un dataframe avec les résultats
  eval_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(evaluations), function(penalty) {
    data.frame(
      penalty = penalty,
      rss = evaluations[[penalty]]$rss,
      bic = evaluations[[penalty]]$bic,
      aic = evaluations[[penalty]]$aic,
      num_changes = evaluations[[penalty]]$num_changes
    )
  }))
  
  # Trouver la meilleure pénalité basée sur le BIC
  best_penalty <- eval_df$penalty[which.min(eval_df$bic)]
  
  # Visualiser les résultats
  p <- ggplot(eval_df, aes(x = penalty)) +
    geom_point(aes(y = bic, color = "BIC")) +
    geom_point(aes(y = aic, color = "AIC")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("BIC" = "blue", "AIC" = "green")) +
    labs(title = "Critères d'information vs Pénalité",
         x = "Pénalité", y = "Valeur du critère") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  
  print(p)
  
  return(list(evaluations = eval_df, best_penalty = best_penalty))
}

# Utilisation
penalties <- c("SIC", "BIC", "AIC", "MBIC", "MAIC", "Hannan-Quinn", "Asymptotic", "Manual")
results <- analyze_changepoints(Burel$vehicle, penalties)

# Afficher les résultats
print(results$evaluations)
cat("Meilleure pénalité:", results$best_penalty)

# Appliquer le modèle final avec la meilleure pénalité
final_model <- cpt.meanvar(Burel$vehicle, method = "PELT", penalty = "MBIC")

# Visualiser les points de rupture
plot(final_model)
```

analyze_segment <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    summarise(
      start_date = first(date),
      end_date = last(date),
      mean_traffic = mean(vehicle),
      sd_traffic = sd(vehicle),
      min_traffic = min(vehicle),
      max_traffic = max(vehicle)
    )
}

# Fonction pour détecter les anomalies dans un segment
detect_anomalies <- function(data) {
  mean_traffic <- mean(data$vehicle)
  sd_traffic <- sd(data$vehicle)
  threshold <- 3 * sd_traffic
  
  data %>%
    mutate(anomaly = ifelse(abs(vehicle - mean_traffic) > threshold, "Yes", "No"))
}

# Appliquer la détection d'anomalies à chaque segment

# Combiner les résultats

# Visualiser les anomalies

  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = df_anomalies[df_anomalies$anomaly == "Yes",], aes(color = "Anomaly"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(data = df_anomalies[df_anomalies$changepoint == "Yes",], aes(color = "Changepoint"), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Anomaly" = "blue", "Changepoint" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Traffic Volume with Changepoints and Anomalies", x = "Date", y = "Vehicle Count")

Comparaison des différentes périodes :
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Créer une liste de segments
segments <- split(df_plot, cumsum(df_plot$changepoint == "Yes"))

# Préparer les données pour le boxplot
boxplot_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(segments), function(i) {
  segment <- segments[[i]]
  segment$period <- i
  return(segment)
}))

# Créer un dataframe avec les informations sur les périodes
period_info <- boxplot_data %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    start_date = min(date),
    end_date = max(date),
    n_days = as.numeric(difftime(max(date), min(date), units = "days"))
  )

# Créer des labels plus explicites pour l'axe des x
period_labels <- paste0( format(period_info$end_date, "%Y-%m-%d"), "\n", format(period_info$start_date, "%Y-%m-%d"))

# Convertir la période en facteur avec les nouveaux labels
boxplot_data$period <- factor(boxplot_data$period, 
                              levels = period_info$period,
                              labels = period_labels)

# Créer le graphique avec boxplots
ggplot(boxplot_data, aes(x = period, y = vehicle)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outlier.colour = "red", outlier.shape = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Comparison of Traffic Periods",
       x = "Period Start Date",
       y = "Vehicle Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, width = 10))

# Afficher les informations détaillées sur les périodes
print(period_info)
```

Détection des anomalies 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Fonction pour détecter les anomalies dans un segment
detect_anomalies <- function(data) {
  mean_traffic <- mean(data$vehicle)
  sd_traffic <- sd(data$vehicle)
  threshold <- 3 * sd_traffic
  
  data %>%
    mutate(anomaly = ifelse(abs(vehicle - mean_traffic) > threshold, "Yes", "No"),
           anomaly_direction = case_when(
             vehicle > mean_traffic + threshold ~ "High",
             vehicle < mean_traffic - threshold ~ "Low",
             TRUE ~ "Normal"
           ))
}

# Appliquer la détection d'anomalies à chaque segment
segments_with_anomalies <- lapply(segments, detect_anomalies)

# Combiner les résultats
df_anomalies <- do.call(rbind, segments_with_anomalies)

# Visualiser les anomalies
ggplot(df_anomalies, aes(x = date, y = vehicle)) +
  geom_line(color = "grey") +
  geom_point(data = df_anomalies[df_anomalies$anomaly == "Yes",], 
             aes(color = anomaly_direction), size = 3) +
  geom_vline(data = df_anomalies[df_anomalies$changepoint == "Yes",], 
             aes(xintercept = date), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("High" = "red", "Low" = "blue", "Normal" = "green")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Traffic Volume with Changepoints and Anomalies", 
       x = "Date", y = "Vehicle Count",
       color = "Anomaly Type") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```



```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(changepoint)

analyze_traffic <- function(data, segment_id) {
  # Filtrer les données pour le segment spécifié
  segment_data <- data %>% filter(segment_id == !!segment_id)

  # Appliquer le modèle PELT avec MBIC
  model_mbic <- cpt.meanvar(segment_data$vehicle, method = "PELT", penalty = "MBIC")
  changepoints <- cpts(model_mbic)
  
  # Créer un dataframe pour la visualisation
  df_plot <- segment_data %>%
    mutate(changepoint = ifelse(row_number() %in% changepoints, "Yes", "No"))
  
  # 1. Plot initial
  plot_initial <- plot(model_mbic)
  
  # 2. Boxplots
  segments <- split(df_plot, cumsum(df_plot$changepoint == "Yes"))
  
  boxplot_data <- map_dfr(seq_along(segments), ~{
    segment <- segments[[.x]]
    segment %>% mutate(period = .x)
  })
  
  period_info <- boxplot_data %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    summarise(
      start_date = min(date),
      end_date = max(date),
      n_days = as.numeric(difftime(max(date), min(date), units = "days"))
    )
  
  period_labels <- paste0(format(period_info$start_date, "%m-%d"), "\n", format(period_info$end_date, "%m-%d"))
  
  boxplot_data$period <- factor(boxplot_data$period, 
                                levels = period_info$period,
                                labels = period_labels)
  
  plot_boxplot <- ggplot(boxplot_data, aes(x = period, y = vehicle)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outlier.colour = "red", outlier.shape = 1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Comparison of Traffic Periods for", segment_id),
         x = "Period Start Date", y = "Vehicle Count") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 10))
  
  # 3. Changepoints with anomalies
  detect_anomalies <- function(data) {
    mean_traffic <- mean(data$vehicle, na.rm = TRUE)
    sd_traffic <- sd(data$vehicle, na.rm = TRUE)
    threshold <- 3 * sd_traffic
    
    data %>%
      mutate(anomaly = ifelse(abs(vehicle - mean_traffic) > threshold, "Yes", "No"),
             anomaly_direction = case_when(
               vehicle > mean_traffic + threshold ~ "High",
               vehicle < mean_traffic - threshold ~ "Low",
               TRUE ~ "Normal"
             ))
  }
  
  segments_with_anomalies <- map(segments, detect_anomalies)
  df_anomalies <- bind_rows(segments_with_anomalies)
  
  # Filtrer uniquement les points anormaux
  df_anomalies_only <- df_anomalies %>% filter(anomaly == "Yes")
  
  # Affichage des anomalies sur la série
  plot_anomalies <- ggplot(df_anomalies, aes(x = date, y = vehicle)) +
    geom_line(color = "grey") +
    geom_point(data = df_anomalies_only, aes(color = anomaly_direction), size = 3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("High" = "red", "Low" = "blue")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Traffic Volume with Anomalies for Segment", segment_id),
         x = "Date", y = "Vehicle Count",
         color = "Anomaly Type") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # Retourner les trois graphiques dans une liste
  return(list(
    initial_plot = plot_initial,
    boxplot = plot_boxplot,
    anomalies_plot = plot_anomalies
  ))
}

# Utilisation de la fonction

# Créer une liste de tous les segment_id uniques
unique_segments <- unique(data_V2$segment_id)

# Initialiser une liste vide pour stocker les résultats
list_result <- list()

# Boucle sur chaque segment_id
for (id in unique_segments) {
  tryCatch({
    results <- analyze_traffic(data_V2, id)
    list_result[[as.character(id)]] <- results
    
    # Afficher les graphiques (optionnel)
    print(results$initial_plot)
    print(results$boxplot)
    print(results$anomalies_plot)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Erreur pour le segment_id", id, ":", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
  })
}

```
